messages.author: 6b3dfa6c2646a8c1
messages.subject: parameterization of additive ICAR model
parts:
Hello,

I am seeking advice about parameterization of ICAR GMRF model. I’m trying to fit a model to incidence by time and age: g(t,a) = f(t) + f(a) + f(t,a), where each of the functions have ICAR(1) priors in one dimension for f(t) and f(a) and two dimensions for f(t,a). The model formulation reflects the expectation that there is a dominant age and time trend, with smaller deviations in the f(a,t) term (in which we are quite interested).

The model fits well when I fit only the additive terms f(t) + f(a), or when I fit only the bivariate function f(t,a), but when I fit the additive model g(t,a) = f(t) + f(a) + f(t,a) the step size becomes very very small, it reaches maximum tree depth, and n_divergent is high. I suspect that the problem may be related to the variance parameter associated with f(t,a) is much smaller than the variance on f(t) and f(a).

The likelihood for the real data is more complicated and computationally expensive, but for the purposes of exploring the model structure I’ve created a simple Poisson likelihood (attached). I’ve parameterized the model in two ways (1) parameterizing the values of the response g(t,a) and applying linear transformations to recover the underlying f(t), f(a), f(t,a), and (2) directly parameterizing f(t), f(a), and f(t,a) [with sum-to-zero constraints for identifiability].

When I simulate random data without any trends (such that the variance for the three additive terms are of similar magnitude), the model converges well and fast. But when I simulate more realistic data, such that the variation in f(t,a) is much less than in f(t) and f(a) dimensions, I get much the same as with the real data -- very small step size, and poor convergence. I’m wondering if anyone has advice for better parameterization of the model? (Or if I’ve done something obviously silly...)

In other threads about GMRFs, I’ve seen suggestions to consider applying the ‘Matt trick’, but wasn’t sure how to apply it to the improper covariance matrix for 2D ICAR(1) prior for f(t,a).

Thanks,
Jeff

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] parameterization of additive ICAR model
parts:
This one's way out of my comfort zone in terms of modeling.
I hope someone else can help on details.

You do want to get all your parameters on the same scale to
the extent possible. Adaptation will help with this, but it's
not perfect. You can try running longer warmup periods (perhaps
starting from a lower stepsize and targeting a higher adapt_delta
[acceptance rate]).

There is a log_mix function that will simplify your transformed
parameters considerably. And given that lp_2 doesn't show up
in the model, that would be better defined in the generated
quantities block as a local variable so you don't need to write
it all out.

Usually you care about expectations, so don't need to actually
sample from the Bernoulli --- all you need to know about it can
be recovered from prob_lp_2. Neat use of softmax in the generated
quantities block, by the way --- I always just did that by hand,
but your way is much better for computing prob_lp_2.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] parameterization of additive ICAR model
parts:
Oops --- this one went to the wrong thread. I must've been
looking at a very old buffer in Xcode.

But my comment stands that I don't know anyting about ICAR
models. Hopefully someone else will be able to take a look.
Given the complexity of that code, I'd suggest writing some
tests with print statements to make sure it's doing what you
expect it to do.

One minor comment: for your model, you should define
rep_vector(1.0/ny, ny) and same for the nx version as constants in
transformed data to avoid recreating this vector every log density eval.

- Bob
